title: The numbers change
subject: Money

text: A course that was right last year can be wrong this year.
The standard deduction, the EITC limits, and the Free File cutoff all move. Treat any printed figure as a year, not a fact.
Tax year is the year you earned the money. Filing year is the year you send the return.
A 2025 return is filed in 2026. A page that says 2026 may mean the return due in 2026, or the money earned in 2026. Read which one.
The standard deduction is indexed. So are the EITC income limits and the maximum credit.
A threshold can also change by law, not just by inflation. The 2025 standard deduction was raised by statute, not only by the usual index.
A blog, a video, or last year's software can quote a dead number with confidence.
If the page does not name the tax year, do not use the number. If it names a year that is not yours, do not use the number.
You see '$15,000 standard deduction for single filers' with no year. What do you do?

choices.label: Do not use it. Find the figure for your tax year on IRS.gov.
Use it. The deduction never changes.
Average it with last year's number.

text: Every figure in this module is for tax year 2025. Next year it may be wrong.
